figures.finding: The Cook Islands have no performer's permit: no one under thirteen may be employed; a school-age person (thirteen to fifteen, unless allowed to leave school) may not be employed during school hours, for more than ten hours a week outside them, or in other than light work, without the Secretary's approval, which is given only if the work raises no educational or safety risk. The rule is for any employment, writing or directing included.

value.permit: approval of the Secretary (Internal Affairs) for school-age persons beyond the limits

sources.said: An employer must not employ a person who is under 13 years of age. An employer must not, without the approval of the Secretary, employ a school-age person— (a) during normal school hours; or (b) for more than 10 hours per week outside normal school hours; or (c) for work other than light work.
The Secretary may only give approval under subsection (2) if satisfied that the employment will not give rise to any educational or occupational safety and health risks to the school-age person.

sources.title: Employment Relations Act 2012 (No. 17 of 2012), section 30, Ministry of Internal Affairs, Cook Islands (scan, read by OCR)
